newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to sell Elk Hills oil field stake in segments.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to sell Elk Hills oil field stake in segments.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department said Tuesday it planned to offer operating and non-operating interests when it sells off its 78 percent stake in the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve.
Under law, the government must sell its interest in the oil and gas field, among the 10 largest in the lower 48 states, by February 1998.

"Bids will be solicited for an 'operating working interest,' where the buyer will become the field's operator, and for multiple, 'non-operating working interests'," the Energy Department's fossil energy office said.
The sale of the Elk Hills field in Bakersfield, California, is expected to be one of the largest U.S. government privatizations ever.

By offering its stake in pieces, the Energy Department said it aimed to increase competition for the field, drawing bids from independent producers and refiners who depend on the light crude oil from Elk Hills for blending with heavier oil.

"If a single purchaser wants to buy the entire operation, its bid will have to exceed the highest bids for all of the individual segments," Assistant Energy Secretary Patricia Fry Godley said in a statement.
The Energy Department said it would hold public meetings in Houston on October 15 and in Bakersfield on October 16 to outline its sales strategy to prospective buyers.
The government plans to start seeking bids for the field in April 1997.
